title: Exposure heatmap + steward rotation playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick working playbook for mapping rollout exposure to a heatmap and operationalizing steward rotations so that signal coverage, escalations, and rollback authority are explicit across cross-functional teams. Not a final policy — this is the lab scratchpad we can iterate from when planning medium-risk LLM feature exposures.

Summary (one-liner):
Create a time-zone-aware heatmap of exposure density (traffic + model-change risk) and align it to a rotating roster of stewards with explicit handoff scripts, short overlap windows, and escalation contacts for each heat level.

Why this exists (context):
- We often launch LL-driven features with distributed teams and unclear evening/overnight ownership.
- Observability gaps show delayed response for transient signal spikes during low-coverage hours.
- Need a lightweight, repeatable ritual that pairs exposure slices to human stewards and reduces time-to-rollback for severe degradation.

Core concepts (draft):
- Exposure heatmap: 2D grid (time-of-day x cohort intensity) where each cell gets a risk score (0-5) based on traffic share, model novelty, user impact, and historical churn.
- Steward band: contiguous time block assigned to a steward pair (primary + backup) responsible for watch, triage, and execution.
- Overlap window: 15-30 minute enforced overlap between adjacent steward bands for handoff.
- Heat levels: Green (0-1), Amber (2-3), Red (4-5) with clear actions per level.

How to build the heatmap (practical):
1) Inputs: expected traffic by cohort (from experiment config), model variant tags, recent regression/safety flags, latency percentiles, token-cost delta.
2) Weighting heuristic (initial): 50% traffic share, 20% model novelty (0/1/2), 15% latency/availability degradation risk, 15% safety/regulatory sensitivity.
3) Normalization: compute per-cell numeric score 0-5, bucket into heat levels.
4) Visual: export CSV -> lightweight heatmap in internal dashboard or simple Google sheet color rules for first pass.

Steward rotation design (ops):
- Shift length: prefer 2–4 hour micro-shifts for high-traffic launches (enables focused attention), otherwise 4–6 hour for steady releases.
- Pairing: primary steward (decider) + secondary (exec/support). Rotate at 2-week cadence for primary pool to reduce fatigue.
- Coverage matrix: map each heatmap cell to a steward pair. Use region-aware assignment to ensure someone is awake.
- Overlap: mandatory 15m handoff notes + quick signal sanity check (see template below).

Handoff script (short template):
- Before overlap end: primary sends 3-line update in #rollouts channel: current heat level, any open incidents (IDs), observed drift metrics, immediate actions taken.
- During overlap: incoming steward verifies alerts up/down, replays the last 50 user traces for cohort X, checks latency tail and error-rate baselines.
- After handoff: outgoing steward pins a short note in the experiment doc: timestamp, major observations, recommended next steps.

Escalation ladder (operational):
- Amber: steward triage -> involve on-call SRE if latency > threshold or error rate > X%.
- Red: immediate rollback authority flows to product steward + SRE oncall. Target Time-To-Rollback (TTR) = 10 minutes.
- Communications: incident bridge + page to product manager, SRE, legal (if data-sensitive). Use templated messages.

Quick checklist for morning-of (launch day):
- Generate heatmap from experiment plan and sanity-check with product & SRE.
- Publish steward roster and contact list in experiment doc and #rollouts.
- Confirm overlap windows and that all stewards have access to diagnostic dashboards, rollback buttons, runbooks.
- Run a 10m dry-run of handoff script pre-launch.

Measurement matrix (what we watch):
- Latency p95/p99 by route and cohort (absolute + delta from baseline).
- Error rate and category breakdown (HTTP 5xx, model timeouts, hallucination flags if available).
- Safety classifier regression count (false positive/negative trends).
- Cost burn rate (tokens/min) vs expected.
- User-facing KPI degradation (conversion, retention signals) if instrumented.

Simulations to run prior to trusting the roster:
- Synthetic spike during low-coverage hours: ensure steward rotation triggers paged handoff and TTR < target.
- Oscillating latency: validate autoscaler and fallback model variant engage and steward runbook works.
- Partial rollback scenario: test canary rollback path end-to-end (config, traffic slicing, rollback metrics).

Open questions / trade-offs (notes-to-self):
- Shift length vs fatigue: micro-shifts increase context-switch cost, longer shifts risk decreased vigilance. Need observational study on response times by shift length.
- Automated vs human escalation: how much can we safely automate (auto-rollback on severe safety classifier hits)? legal/risk might require human-in-loop.
- Cross-team ownership: for small customers, steward pool may be 1 person covering many launches. Is that acceptable?

Operational templates (snippets):
- Slack ping template: "STEWARD-ALERT: [cohort] heat=[level] key-metric=[p99 1.8s -> 2.6s] action-needed=[triage/rollback] link=[doc]"
- Handoff note template (paste into experiment doc): "handoff: out=<name> in=<name> time=<ISO> heat=<level> actions=<short list> open_incidents=[IDs]"

Next steps (concrete):
- Aisha: prototype the sheet + color rules and export a sample heatmap for the upcoming reranker canary (due 2025-10-02).
- Marco: simulate spike scenario with traffic-faker and measure TTR for 2h vs 4h shifts (deadline 2025-10-09).
- Lina: align SRE on escalation thresholds and add them to the runbook (deadline 2025-10-07).
- Me (Riley): consolidate simulation results and propose default steward cadence for beta launches by 2025-10-15.

Appendix: quick risk scoring rubric (first-pass)
- Traffic share: 0 (0%), 1 (0-1%), 2 (1-5%), 3 (5-15%), 4 (15-40%), 5 (40%+)
- Model novelty: 0 (no change), 2 (tuning), 4 (new model family)
- Latency/availability risk: 0-5 scaled to expected p99 delta and error rate increase
- Safety/regulatory sensitivity: 0 (none) to 5 (PII/financial/legal exposure)

Notes-to-self (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep initial system simple: sheet + Slack + short roster. If it proves reliable, invest in dashboard + automated mapping.
- Consider a lightweight hourly digest for stewards during low-heat windows to reduce alert fatigue.
- Think about using roster as an explicit training signal for new oncall stewards so they get experience with half-day micro-launches.

Related docs to consult:
- rollout-ops-pocket-guide (conductor)
- canary-human-factor-observatory notes (we have behavioral insight that small rotations reduce missed signals)

-- end draft --

This is intentionally terse and rough. Use as a seed for the runbook doc proper.
